title: 🌑 Lunar Occultation — Moon covers Regulus
description:
The Moon passes directly in front of the star Regulus (magnitude +1.4), briefly hiding it from view. This is a lunar occultation — one of the most dramatic naked-eye astronomical events, since the target disappears almost instantaneously behind the Moon's limb and reappears just as suddenly.

The just-past-full Moon (98% illuminated) passes in front of Regulus, the brightest star in Leo. The event occurs in daylight for much of the eastern US — use binoculars to find the Moon in the blue sky and watch Regulus blink out at the Moon's dark limb.

Visible from: Eastern North America, including the eastern United States and eastern Canada.

Disappears: 08:45 UTC
Reappears: 09:40 UTC

The waning gibbous Moon (67% illuminated) occults Regulus in the pre-dawn sky. Regulus vanishes behind the Moon's bright limb and reappears from the dark limb, making the reappearance sudden and dramatic. Best viewed from a dark site before morning twilight brightens the sky.

Visible from: Central and eastern North America, parts of Europe.

title: 🌑 Lunar Occultation — Moon covers Venus
description:
The Moon passes directly in front of Venus (magnitude -4.5), briefly hiding it from view. This is a lunar occultation — one of the most dramatic naked-eye astronomical events, since the target disappears almost instantaneously behind the Moon's limb and reappears just as suddenly.

One of the year's most striking events: the crescent Moon (14% illuminated) covers brilliant Venus in the evening sky. Venus shines at magnitude −4.5, making it visible even in twilight. Watch for Venus to disappear behind the Moon's dark limb and reappear dramatically from the bright limb. This is a naked-eye event — no equipment needed, though binoculars enhance the view considerably.

Visible from: Contiguous United States, Canada, Brazil, and Venezuela.

Disappears: 20:10 UTC
Reappears: 21:05 UTC

title: 🌑 Lunar Occultation — Moon covers Venus
description:
The Moon passes directly in front of Venus (magnitude -4.2), briefly hiding it from view. This is a lunar occultation — one of the most dramatic naked-eye astronomical events, since the target disappears almost instantaneously behind the Moon's limb and reappears just as suddenly.

A daytime occultation of Venus by the crescent Moon, visible from Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East. Venus at magnitude −4.2 is bright enough to spot with binoculars in a blue sky near the Moon. The event occurs in the afternoon, so the Moon and Venus will be well above the horizon for the visibility region.

Visible from: Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East.

Disappears: 14:30 UTC
Reappears: 15:25 UTC

title: 🌑 Lunar Occultation — Moon covers Jupiter
description:
The Moon passes directly in front of Jupiter (magnitude -2.9), briefly hiding it from view. This is a lunar occultation — one of the most dramatic naked-eye astronomical events, since the target disappears almost instantaneously behind the Moon's limb and reappears just as suddenly.

The waning gibbous Moon (96% illuminated) covers Jupiter in the pre-dawn sky. Jupiter shines at magnitude −2.9 near opposition, making it one of the brightest objects in the sky. Disappearance occurs at the Moon's bright limb and reappearance at the dark limb — the sudden reappearance is particularly dramatic. Observers with small telescopes can watch Jupiter's moons emerge one by one as the planet reappears.

Visible from: Most of North America (excluding the far western US), northern Cuba.

Disappears: 05:15 UTC
Reappears: 06:20 UTC

title: 🌑 Lunar Occultation — Moon covers Mars
description:
The Moon passes directly in front of Mars (magnitude -1.1), briefly hiding it from view. This is a lunar occultation — one of the most dramatic naked-eye astronomical events, since the target disappears almost instantaneously behind the Moon's limb and reappears just as suddenly.

The waxing crescent Moon occults Mars in the evening sky for observers across Europe and North Africa. Mars is near opposition and shining at magnitude −1.1, making it an unmistakably bright reddish-orange object. The dark-limb disappearance is visible to the naked eye.

Visible from: Europe, North Africa.

Disappears: 22:50 UTC
Reappears: 23:45 UTC
